newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Nobel prize brought more suffering to E.Timor - Belo.
newsitem.headline: Nobel prize brought more suffering to E.Timor - Belo.

text.p: Bishop Carlos Ximenes Belo was quoted as saying that the award of his 1996 Nobel peace prize had brought more suffering to the Timorese and that torture and arrests had increased in the Pacific territory.

The award of the prize in October 1996 "brought much suffering for the young people (of Timor)," the Portuguese news agency Lusa quoted Belo, bishop of Dili, as saying at a dinner in his honour in the southern Algarve region on Thursday night.
"The number of cases of arrests and torture among the youngest in the territory has increased," he added.
"Many were questioned, tortured and some were imprisoned (by the Indonesian authorities), just because they shouted 'Long live the Nobel', 'Long live Ximenes'," Belo said.
In Lisbon on Wednesday, Bishop Belo said the award of the prize had not contributed to ending suffering in East Timor.

Belo, who wasd in Portugal to attend ceremonies at the Catholic shrine of Fatima marking the 80th anniversary of the "apparition" of the Virgin Mary to three Portuguese children, won the prize with Timor resistance leader Jose Ramos Horta.

Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in December 1975 and still maintains a heavy military presence there. It unilaterally annexed the territory in July 1976 in an act not recognised by the United Nations.
